node.statement: The epsilon=0 limit from 1.4 is dagger-preserving and has extended defect zero. Indeed every v_j for j>=1 is dagger-preserving and the involution is isometric, so that identity passes to the operator-norm limit. At each fixed amplification, the two-sided (1+-d_j) norm bounds pass to the limit as d_j tends to zero. The d_j-homomorphism defect inequalities also pass to the limit because multiplication is continuous at every matrix level in the extended 0-C*-algebra (the product-norm axiom gives ||XY||<=||X||||Y||). Thus every v_tilde_n=I_n tensor v_tilde is a 0-homomorphism satisfying exact two-sided norm bounds, i.e. v_tilde is an extended 0-inclusion, and its extended defect is 0=K_floor epsilon.
